hero.headline: Trump confirms profanity-laced call with Netanyahu over Lebanon
hero.body:
President Trump publicly confirmed Wednesday that he had a heated conversation with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, using strong language to express his frustration over Israel's military operations in Lebanon. Trump made the acknowledgment during an appearance on the New York Post podcast hosted by Miranda Devine.

When Devine asked if Trump had called Netanyahu "fucking crazy" and suggested he would face prison without Trump's support, the president responded affirmatively. "I did," Trump said. "I wouldn't say angry. I was a little bit perturbed at his constantly fighting with Lebanon, you know. At some point I said, 'Bibi, we've got to stop this. We gotta stop it.'"

Trump noted that despite the tension, he maintains positive feelings toward Netanyahu and has worked well with him historically. The conversation reflected Trump's effort to curb Israel's intensified military campaign in the region as he seeks to manage broader tensions with Iran.

The call reveals a significant shift in the public relationship between the two leaders. Trump's willingness to confirm the details rather than deny or minimize the report demonstrates his administration's readiness to apply pressure on Israel regarding its military conduct in Lebanon. Trump appears to view his past support for Netanyahu as leverage in current negotiations.

The exchange occurs amid a complex regional situation. Iran had threatened to suspend peace talks with the United States over Israel's offensive actions in Lebanon. Trump, eager to prevent further escalation and secure a path away from direct confrontation with Iran, reportedly used the profanity-laden call to push Netanyahu toward de-escalation.

The death toll in Lebanon has mounted significantly during the conflict with Israel, reaching 1,422 people according to Lebanese health ministry data. In the 24 hours preceding reports of this call, Israeli strikes killed 54 people and wounded 156 others. These figures underscore the intensity of the military operations that prompted Trump's criticism.

The disagreement over Lebanon marks a notable departure from the strong alignment between Trump and Netanyahu during Trump's first presidency. That period saw the U.S. embassy relocated to Jerusalem and the brokering of the Abraham Accords, which normalized relations between Israel and several Arab nations.

Trump's public confirmation of the tense exchange, rather than attempting to suppress or reframe the story, suggests a calculated diplomatic strategy. By acknowledging the call and his criticism, Trump appears to be signaling to regional actors that he is willing to distance himself from Israeli military decisions when necessary. This approach could serve his effort to prevent further escalation with Iran while maintaining the broader U.S.-Israel relationship.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes as Iranian drones hit Kuwait airport, killing one
cards.body:
The United States and Iran escalated their military confrontation with a new round of strikes, as Iranian drones damaged Kuwait's international airport and killed one person.

The attack on Kuwait's airport terminal occurred after the US military disabled an Iranian oil tanker in the strait of Hormuz. American forces fired a missile at the Botswana-flagged M/T Lexie on Tuesday after its crew ignored repeated warnings over 24 hours. The ship was heading toward Iran's Kharg Island when the strike disabled its engine.

In response, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps launched drones that struck a passenger terminal at Kuwait's international airport on Wednesday, wounding several people and forcing authorities to suspend air traffic. Kuwait's defense ministry described the attack as "criminal Iranian aggression which resulted in significant material damage to the building and injuries." Civil aviation authorities transferred arriving flights to alternative airports following the strikes.

The Iranian military claimed it attacked the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain with missiles and drones in retaliation for the strike on Qeshm Island, though US Central Command denied this claim. American forces said they shot down three Iranian attack drones launched toward civilian ships in regional waters and conducted strikes on an Iranian military ground control station on Qeshm Island.

The IRGC stated that the US strike on an Iranian oil tanker damaged the vessel's engine room, calling the incident an example of "aggressive US military" action.

The latest exchange represents a significant setback to ceasefire negotiations. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed this week that a deal with Iran was within reach and that Tehran had agreed to discuss nuclear program aspects previously off the table. However, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi signaled that Iran would suspend peace talks with the US to protest Israeli military operations in Lebanon, stating that "the ceasefire between Iran and the US is unequivocally a ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon."

The situation has grown more complex with Lebanon's involvement. Despite Trump's announcement that he had stopped an imminent Israeli strike on Beirut and secured agreement from Israel and Hezbollah to end fighting, Israeli warplanes conducted 30 strikes across southern Lebanon on Tuesday alone. Rescuers recovered six bodies from one strike near Sidon, including two children.

The tanker strike marked the sixth ship disabled by US forces since April 13, when the military began its blockade of Iran. US forces have redirected 122 vessels attempting to enter or exit Iranian ports. Over the weekend, US forces had struck Iranian radar and drone sites, prompting Iran to target a military base in Kuwait it claimed was involved in the operation.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise as U.S. and Iran Exchange Strikes
cards.body:
Oil prices climbed after Iranian drones struck Kuwait's main international airport and the United States and Iran exchanged military strikes in the Persian Gulf region. The escalating hostilities have undermined fragile ceasefire negotiations between Washington and Tehran, creating uncertainty about the trajectory of the conflict.

Kuwait shut down its main airport temporarily after Iranian drones heavily damaged civilian buildings at the facility, killing at least one person. The attack represented a significant escalation in the ongoing military confrontation between the two countries. The U.S. military responded by firing on Iranian sites, including locations on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps claimed it attacked the U.S. Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain with missiles and drones in response, though the U.S. military's Central Command denied the attack was successful.

The strikes come as both countries were pursuing ceasefire discussions. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed on Tuesday that a deal with Tehran was within reach and asserted that Iran had agreed to negotiate aspects of its nuclear program previously off the table. However, the Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi countered that the ceasefire agreement covered all fronts in the region, including Lebanon, and that violations on any front constituted breaches of the entire agreement.

The Persian Gulf region remains critical to global oil supplies, and military conflict near major production and shipping routes has immediate effects on energy markets. The Strait of Hormuz, where the U.S. had reportedly fired a Hellfire missile at a tanker attempting to break through an American blockade, is particularly sensitive to disruptions. Traders responded to the overnight hostilities by bidding up crude prices as concerns mounted about potential disruptions to energy shipments.

The exchange of strikes underscores the precarious state of U.S.-Iran relations despite diplomatic claims of progress. The simultaneous pursuit of negotiations while conducting direct military operations creates significant uncertainty about whether the ceasefire will hold. Kuwait, a key U.S. ally in the region, now finds itself directly affected by the escalating confrontation between the two powers.

The oil market reaction demonstrates how quickly energy supplies can be threatened when military conflict occurs near major production and shipping infrastructure. Energy traders are closely monitoring developments, aware that further escalation could have broader economic consequences beyond immediate price increases. The attack on Kuwait's airport also raises concerns about the safety of civilian infrastructure as the conflict intensifies.

Analysts are watching both the military situation and diplomatic progress closely, as the outcome will likely determine whether oil prices stabilize or face additional pressure in coming weeks.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran agreed to not have nuclear weapons but could reverse decision
cards.teaser: President Trump said Iran has agreed to not develop nuclear weapons, but cautioned the agreement could be reversed.
cards.body:
President Trump stated that Iran has agreed to forgo nuclear weapons development. However, he added a caveat that the Iranian government could change its position on the commitment.

The remarks come as reports indicate a draft US-Iran plan is under discussion. Trump also said Democrats and some Republicans he described as unpatriotic are complicating negotiations with Iran.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Announces Tariffs on 59 Countries Over Forced Labor
cards.teaser: The administration plans levies up to 12.5 percent on countries that failed to crack down on goods made with forced labor.
cards.body:
The Trump administration plans to impose tariffs between 10 and 12.5 percent on 60 trading partners, including the UK, EU, Canada, Taiwan, and Australia. The levies target countries that officials claim have not adequately addressed forced labor in manufacturing.

The announcement follows a February Supreme Court ruling that invalidated many of Trump's previous tariffs. By framing these duties around forced labor concerns, the administration is attempting to use different legal grounds to reinstate trade penalties after the court limited its earlier tariff authority. The EU has already objected, stating the move breaches the spirit of a tariff agreement reached last July.

cards.headline: Ukraine Strikes St. Petersburg as Putin Economic Forum Opens
cards.teaser: Ukrainian drones hit a navy base and oil terminal in the region that includes Russia's second-largest city.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck oil storage facilities and energy infrastructure near St. Petersburg on Wednesday morning, hours before international delegates arrived for Russia's flagship economic forum. Russian air defenses attempted to intercept the long-range drones, but several reached their targets, causing explosions and fires visible across the city.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had targeted a navy base and oil terminal in the region. The timing of the attacks coincided with the opening of the annual economic conference, where Putin was scheduled to address business leaders and government officials on Friday.

cards.headline: White House moves to take control of billions in federal science grants
cards.teaser: The White House Office of Management and Budget is working to control billions of dollars in federal research grants, prompting concerns about scientific independence.
cards.body:
The White House Office of Management and Budget has proposed sweeping policy changes that would require Trump-appointed officials to vet all federal grants issued to universities and nongovernmental organizations. Under the proposal, grants must "demonstrably advance the president's policy priorities" and align with "American values" as defined by the president.

Scientists and experts have raised broad alarm about the changes, warning the proposal would deal a devastating blow to American science. Critics argue that allowing political appointees to influence grant decisions threatens the independence and integrity of federally funded research.

hero.headline: Iranian Attack on Kuwait Airport Kills One as U.S.-Iran Conflict Escalates
hero.body:
An Iranian drone strike on Kuwait's international airport killed one person and wounded several others, according to Kuwaiti military officials. The attack damaged a passenger terminal and forced authorities to suspend air traffic and redirect arriving flights to alternative airports.

The strike represents a dangerous escalation in the conflict between the United States and Iran, bringing direct military action against a country that hosts American military personnel and maintains close security ties with Washington. Brigadier General Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan, Kuwait's defense ministry spokesperson, described the attack as "criminal Iranian aggression which resulted in significant material damage to the building and injuries."

The airport strike came as part of a broader exchange of military action between the two countries. The sequence began when U.S. forces fired a missile to disable the M/T Lexie, a Botswana-flagged tanker, as it moved through international waters toward Iran's Kharg Island north of the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Central Command said the crew had ignored repeated warnings over 24 hours. The military described the tanker as unladen and said it was attempting to break through an American blockade of the strait that began in April.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps responded to the strike on the tanker by attacking Kuwait's airport with drones. The IRGC also claimed it struck the U.S. Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain with missiles and drones, though U.S. Central Command denied this claim. American forces subsequently reported shooting down three Iranian attack drones launched toward civilian vessels in regional waters and conducted strikes on an Iranian military ground control station on Qeshm Island.

The tit-for-tat exchanges threaten negotiations between Washington and Tehran to establish a ceasefire. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told the Senate Foreign Relations Committee that a deal with Iran appeared within reach and claimed the regime had agreed to discuss aspects of its nuclear program previously off limits.

However, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi signaled that Tehran may suspend peace talks with the United States. He stated that the ceasefire between the two countries must extend to all fronts, including Lebanon, and said violations on any front constitute violations of the entire agreement. His comments reflected Iranian objections to Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon, where dozens of airstrikes have continued despite a supposed ceasefire agreement.

The latest exchanges represent ongoing tensions despite diplomatic claims. This marks the sixth vessel the U.S. military has disabled since the blockade began, with American forces redirecting 122 vessels seeking to enter or exit Iranian ports.

cards.teaser: Ukrainian drones hit a navy base and oil terminal in the region that includes Russia's second-largest city.

Ukrainian drones struck oil storage facilities and energy infrastructure near St. Petersburg on Wednesday morning, hours before international delegates arrived for Russia's flagship economic forum. Russian air defenses attempted to intercept the long-range drones, but several reached their targets, causing explosions and fires visible across the city.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had targeted a navy base and oil terminal in the region. The timing of the attacks coincided with the opening of the annual economic conference, where Putin was scheduled to address business leaders and government officials on Friday.

cards.headline: At Least 21 Killed in Delhi Fire, Including Foreign Nationals
cards.teaser: Many victims were South Asians who had traveled to India for medical treatment or to accompany relatives.
cards.body:
A fire in Delhi has claimed at least 21 lives, with foreign nationals among the victims. Many of those killed were South Asians who had come to India for medical treatment or to support family members receiving care.

The incident ranks among the deadliest fires to strike India's capital in recent months. Delhi has faced multiple major fires in residential and commercial buildings, often attributed to safety code violations and inadequate fire prevention measures in older structures.

cards.headline: Eight Killed After Drone Hits Bus in Russian-Controlled Ukraine
cards.teaser: The bus was traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Russian-controlled Crimea.
cards.body:
A drone strike hit a bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Russian-controlled Crimea, killing eight people, according to Russian officials. The bus was operating on a route connecting the Russian capital with the peninsula that Russia annexed from Ukraine in 2014.

The attack targeted civilian transportation infrastructure in territory under Russian control as the conflict continues.

cards.headline: Protests Over U.K. Murder Case Turn Violent, 11 Officers Injured
cards.teaser: Demonstrators pelted police with rocks and garbage cans during protests over the Henry Nowak murder case.
cards.body:
Violent clashes erupted during protests in the United Kingdom over the murder of teenager Henry Nowak. Demonstrators threw rocks and garbage cans at police officers, leaving eleven injured. Prime Minister Keir Starmer condemned the attacks on police as "disgraceful," while a British cabinet minister described the scenes as "unacceptable."

The unrest occurred in the Southampton community, where residents had gathered to demonstrate over Nowak's stabbing death. British leaders called for an end to the violence as authorities worked to restore order.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes New Tariffs on 60 Countries Over Forced Labor
cards.teaser: The proposal includes a 10 percent tariff on Canada, Mexico, and the European Union.
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% on approximately 60 trading partners, including the UK, EU, Canada, Australia, and Taiwan. The administration cited forced labor concerns in global supply chains as justification for the levies.

The EU immediately rejected the tariffs, arguing they violated the spirit of a trade agreement reached in July. The proposed tariffs represent a broad expansion of U.S. trade enforcement actions and could impact billions of dollars in international commerce.

cards.headline: Iranian Drones Damage Kuwait's Main Airport in Regional Strike
cards.teaser: The attack on the international airport came as Iran continues to target U.S. allies in the Persian Gulf.
cards.body:
Iranian drones struck Kuwait's international airport and other civilian buildings, killing at least one person and injuring dozens, according to local authorities. The attack disrupted operations at the major regional transportation hub.

The strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain were part of escalating exchanges between the US and Iran. Both countries host American military personnel and maintain close security ties with the United States. President Trump indicated that peace talks involving Iran's supreme leader are ongoing.

cards.headline: Trump endorsement fails as farmer defeats congressman in Iowa governor primary
cards.teaser: A farmer backed by a health-focused political movement defeated Trump's endorsed candidate for Iowa governor in a primary upset.
cards.body:
Congressman Randy Feenstra conceded defeat in Iowa's Republican primary for governor after receiving President Trump's endorsement. He lost to Lahn, a farmer backed by a MAHA-affiliated political movement. The result marks a notable setback for Trump's endorsement in the Republican primary race.

Iowa was among six states that held primary elections, with polls closing throughout the evening and results coming in from multiple contests across the country.

cards.headline: Justice Department scraps Trump administration anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: The Justice Department canceled plans for a $1.8 billion fund that would have compensated people the Trump administration deemed politically targeted.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has ended plans for a $1.8 billion fund designed to compensate individuals the Trump administration believed were unjustly targeted for political reasons.

The decision to scrap the fund represents another instance of Republicans pushing back against Trump administration initiatives. The compensation program would have addressed cases the administration viewed as wrongful political persecution.

cards.headline: Karen Bass to face runoff election against Spencer Pratt for Los Angeles mayor
cards.teaser: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass will compete in a runoff election after facing a strong challenge from Spencer Pratt in the primary.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass did not secure an outright victory in the primary election and will advance to a runoff in November. She finished ahead of her opponents but fell short of the 50% threshold needed to win outright.

Bass will face either Spencer Pratt, a former reality TV star, or city council member Nithya Raman in the general election. As of Tuesday evening, the race between Pratt and Raman to claim the second runoff spot remained undecided.

cards.headline: White House moves to take control of billions in federal science grants
cards.teaser: The White House Office of Management and Budget is working to control billions of dollars in federal research grants, prompting concerns about scientific independence.

Under the proposal, grants must "demonstrably advance the president's policy priorities" and align with "American values" as defined by the president.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike oil facilities near St Petersburg ahead of Putin forum
cards.teaser: Several long-range Ukrainian drones hit oil storage facilities near St Petersburg ahead of Vladimir Putin's flagship economic forum.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck oil storage facilities and an oil terminal near St Petersburg, setting at least one facility ablaze. The attacks occurred as the city hosted Putin's annual economic forum, days before the Russian president is scheduled to address the event.

The strikes demonstrate the extended range of Ukrainian drone operations, reaching Russia's second-largest city. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the attacks on the oil infrastructure.

cards.headline: CBS News Fires Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: The former CBS Evening News anchor was ousted after months of tensions between staff and the network's editor in chief.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes after he clashed with network management over recent staff cuts. Pelley, who joined the show in 2004 and previously anchored CBS Evening News, was dismissed following a heated meeting where he criticized the network's decisions.

The conflict erupted after CBS News terminated the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents, Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi. During a staff meeting, Pelley directly challenged editor-in-chief Bari Weiss over the sweeping overhaul, accusing her of "murdering" the news program.

cards.headline: Lloyds Banking Group Apps Hit by Outage
cards.teaser: Users of Lloyds, Halifax and Bank of Scotland mobile apps experienced service disruptions.
cards.body:
Customers of Lloyds Bank, Halifax and Bank of Scotland experienced disruptions to their mobile apps and online banking services. All three banks are part of Lloyds Banking Group, one of the UK's largest financial institutions.

Lloyds Bank acknowledged the issue on X, stating: "We're aware some customers are having issues with our app and online banking. We're really sorry about this."

cards.headline: Macy's Reports Strongest Quarterly Growth in Four Years
cards.teaser: The retailer posted its best first-quarter performance since 2022 and raised its full-year guidance.
cards.body:
Macy's delivered its best first-quarter performance in four years, prompting the company to raise its full-year financial guidance. The department store chain achieved solid results across all three of its brands during the period.

The stronger-than-expected quarterly showing signals that Macy's turnaround strategy is working as the retailer adapts to evolving market conditions and consumer behavior.

cards.headline: European Union Plans to Reduce Reliance on American Technology
cards.teaser: The 27-nation bloc outlined efforts to expand its own data centers, semiconductors and cloud computing capabilities.
cards.body:
The European Union is moving to build greater technological independence from the United States. The 27-nation bloc aims to expand its own data centers, semiconductor production, and cloud computing infrastructure rather than depending heavily on American providers.

This strategic shift reflects Europe's desire for technological sovereignty and resilience. By developing domestic capabilities, the EU seeks to reduce vulnerability to disruptions in transatlantic tech supply chains and strengthen its competitive position in critical technology sectors.

cards.headline: Trump White House Increases Oversight of AI Models
cards.teaser: The administration is finding it needs greater oversight of powerful new artificial intelligence systems despite its industry-friendly stance.
cards.body:
President Trump signed a revised executive order on artificial intelligence that requires voluntary prerelease government reviews of advanced models. The order emerged after industry objections to stricter oversight measures, resulting in a narrower approach than initially proposed.

The shift reflects the administration's effort to balance AI regulation with industry preferences. Rather than mandatory requirements, the executive order relies on companies voluntarily submitting their most powerful AI systems for government review before public release.

hero.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft launch RTX Spark laptops with AI chip architecture
hero.body:
Nvidia has unveiled the RTX Spark, a new processor designed to bring advanced AI capabilities directly to consumer laptops and desktop computers. The chip represents the company's most significant push into the personal computer market and will pit Nvidia against established rivals including Intel, Apple, Qualcomm, and AMD.

The RTX Spark combines a microprocessor and graphics chip, developed in collaboration with Taiwan's MediaTek. Rather than relying on cloud computing, the chip runs AI agents locally on devices. According to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, this architecture will enable AI agents to navigate computers autonomously, potentially replacing traditional mouse and keyboard interactions. "We are reimagining the PC for the first time in 40 years," Huang said at the Computex conference in Taiwan.

The collaboration between Nvidia and Microsoft spans three years and will see the RTX Spark integrated into devices from major manufacturers including Dell, Lenovo, Asus, and HP. The chips will work alongside Microsoft's Windows software, with the companies positioning this partnership as marking the beginning of an era focused on personal AI applications. Despite the chip's powerful capabilities, Nvidia emphasizes that computers using RTX Spark will remain thin and light.

Neil Shah, a co-founder of Counterpoint Research, characterized the RTX Spark moment as comparable to transformative technology launches like the iPhone and ChatGPT. "The RTX Spark looks to transform the traditional app-centric PC to a real useful agentic AI personal computer which will eventually be in every home in coming years as private edge AI agents become pivotal," Shah said.

This move extends Nvidia's reach well beyond its traditional focus on graphics cards and data center processors. The company already dominates AI infrastructure used in large-scale computing facilities, and the consumer chip line allows the company to establish presence across multiple layers of the AI technology ecosystem.

Nvidia is also developing the Vera CPU, designed specifically for AI agents. Early adopters include OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX. The company's expansion into consumer and CPU products signals a strategic shift toward positioning itself as a comprehensive AI solutions provider.

Industry analysts note that while the RTX Spark represents a strategically significant move, its impact on Nvidia's near-term earnings may be limited. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, called it "a longer-term growth opportunity rather than an immediate earnings driver," emphasizing that Nvidia's near-term fortunes remain tied to ongoing demand for data center computing power.

The RTX Spark will launch later this year, opening a new competitive front in the semiconductor industry as companies race to capture the consumer AI market.

cards.headline: Google purchases code from Play Store developers for AI training
cards.teaser: Google has been acquiring source code from Android app developers to use as training material for artificial intelligence models.
cards.body:
Google is compensating Android developers for access to their application source code to train artificial intelligence systems. Through the Play Store platform, developers have received offers to sell their code to Google as part of the company's effort to expand its machine learning datasets with real-world applications.

The practice reflects Google's broader AI investment strategy. Parent company Alphabet recently announced plans to raise $80 billion in equity funding to support its artificial intelligence infrastructure expansion, underscoring the significant resources the tech giant is dedicating to AI development.

cards.headline: Google releases Fitbit Air design files for custom accessories
cards.teaser: Google has published CAD drawings and specifications for the Fitbit Air, enabling third-party manufacturers and individuals to create compatible bands and accessories.
cards.body:
Google released complete blueprints for its Fitbit Air fitness tracker, including CAD drawings and technical specifications that allow anyone to design and produce accessories for the device. The documentation supports manufacturing of items ranging from watch bands to bicep straps for the wearable.

DC Rainmaker reported that the specifications explicitly welcome bicep band designs, while Engadget noted the files enable 3D printing of custom accessories. The move opens the Fitbit Air ecosystem to independent creators and small manufacturers who can now build products without requiring proprietary licensing from Google.

cards.headline: Xcimer activates largest privately owned laser for fusion research
cards.teaser: Fusion energy startup Xcimer has successfully powered up what is now the world's largest laser facility operated by a private company.
cards.body:
Xcimer Energy fired up a laser system that surpasses all other privately owned laser installations in size and power output. The facility will support the company's research into fusion energy generation, which attempts to replicate the energy production process that powers the sun.

The laser activation marks a milestone for private sector fusion research, an area that has historically been dominated by government-funded laboratories. Xcimer joins a growing group of startups working to commercialize fusion power as a clean energy source.

cards.headline: Microsoft announces Linux tools and RTX Spark desktop for developers
cards.teaser: Microsoft revealed plans to bring Linux development tools to Windows and will offer a desktop computer powered by RTX Spark processors aimed at software developers.
cards.body:
Microsoft outlined several developer-focused initiatives at its Build conference, including improved Linux tool integration for Windows and a desktop computer equipped with Nvidia's RTX Spark chips. The desktop will target programmers who need AI processing capabilities on their development machines.

The Linux tools announcement continues Microsoft's years-long effort to make Windows a viable platform for developers who work across multiple operating systems. The RTX Spark desktop extends the laptop launch into workstation territory, providing developers with more powerful hardware options for AI application development.

cards.headline: Uber catalogs thousands of items left behind in robotaxis
cards.teaser: Uber has recovered thousands of forgotten belongings from its autonomous vehicles, ranging from Squishmallow toys to dentures and novelty bags.
cards.body:
Uber's autonomous taxi service has accumulated a large collection of items that passengers left behind in robot-driven cars. The company has been tracking and storing the forgotten belongings, which include stuffed animals, dental appliances, and bags with various printed messages.

Despite the vehicles operating without human drivers, Uber still maintains staff responsible for retrieving and returning lost property. The catalog of forgotten items suggests passengers treat robotaxis similarly to traditional ride services when it comes to leaving personal belongings behind.

cards.headline: Bean plants recruit wasps to attack caterpillars eating their leaves
cards.teaser: Researchers have found that bean plants emit specific chemicals when being eaten by caterpillars, attracting parasitic wasps that prey on the insects.
cards.body:
Bean plants deploy a chemical defense system when under attack from caterpillars, releasing compounds that draw in parasitic wasps. The wasps then target the caterpillars, effectively ending the threat to the plant. The plants use an immune receptor to detect the feeding damage and trigger the chemical signal.

The discovery reveals how plants actively defend themselves rather than passively enduring herbivore damage. The chemical communication between plants and beneficial insects represents a form of biological pest control that occurs naturally in agricultural and wild settings.

hero.headline: Rams acquire Myles Garrett from Browns in blockbuster trade
hero.body:
The Los Angeles Rams acquired star edge rusher Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks. The trade represents one of the most significant defensive player acquisitions in recent NFL history.

Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since the Browns selected him with the first overall pick in 2017, he has established himself as one of the league's premier defensive players. He holds the record for most sacks (125.5), pressures (413), and tackles for loss (149) among all players since his draft year. In 2025, he set a single-season sacks record with 23.

Garrett had requested a trade from the Browns in 2024 after the team finished with a 3-14 record. He stated he wanted to play for a team with a realistic championship opportunity. Despite his trade request, he signed a four-year extension worth $160 million in 2024, making him the highest-paid non-quarterback in the league at that time. The deal included $122.8 million in guaranteed money and an average annual salary of $40 million.

The Browns finished the 2025 season with a 5-12 record and missed the playoffs for the second consecutive year, though Garrett earned All-Pro recognition as the team's lone standout performer. Head coach Kevin Stefanski was fired in January and replaced by Todd Monken, the former Baltimore Ravens offensive coordinator.

General manager Andrew Berry made the deal possible after the Browns and Garrett agreed to modify his contract in March, deferring option payments over the 2026-2028 seasons. This restructuring allowed both sides to move forward with the trade.

"As discussions intensified we were stuck at a legitimate crossroads: do we hold on to a truly generational player who has become the identity of our team, or do we make the difficult decision that we think is best for the organization over the long run?" Berry said following the trade announcement.

The Browns received Verse, a 2027 first-round selection, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round selection. Verse, 25, was a first-round pick by the Rams in 2024 and earned Defensive Rookie of the Year honors. He was selected to the Pro Bowl this past season with 12 career sacks and 22 tackles for loss.

The Rams, who lost to the eventual champion Seattle Seahawks in last season's NFC championship game, have a history of making significant trades. In 2021, they acquired Matthew Stafford from Detroit and won the Super Bowl in his first season. Garrett's arrival brings together the reigning NFL MVP and Defensive Player of the Year as teammates for the first time, as Stafford won his first MVP award last season.

cards.headline: Caleb Williams named Madden NFL 27 cover athlete
cards.teaser: The Chicago Bears quarterback was revealed as the cover athlete for the upcoming video game release.
cards.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was named the cover athlete for Madden NFL 27. Williams described the selection as fulfilling a childhood dream.

The announcement sparked renewed discussion of the so-called Madden curse, a superstition suggesting that players featured on the game's cover experience poor performance or injuries in the following season. Williams becomes the latest NFL player to receive the honor, which has become one of the most recognizable endorsements in sports gaming.

cards.headline: Charles Leclerc signs new long-term contract with Ferrari
cards.teaser: The Ferrari driver agreed to a contract extension ahead of this weekend's Monaco Grand Prix.
cards.body:
Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc has signed a new multiyear contract with the Italian team, securing his future with the Scuderia. The 28-year-old Monegasque will continue driving alongside Lewis Hamilton, who also holds a long-term deal with Ferrari.

The announcement came ahead of this weekend's Monaco Grand Prix, Leclerc's home race. Since joining Ferrari in 2019, Leclerc has competed in 155 races for the team—a tally second only to Michael Schumacher's record during his dominant Ferrari tenure from 1996 to 2006.

cards.headline: Qualifier Maja Chwalinska reaches French Open semifinals
cards.teaser: The qualifier advanced to her first Grand Slam semifinal with a victory over Anna Kalinskaya.
cards.body:
Qualifier Maja Chwalinska defeated Anna Kalinskaya to reach her first Grand Slam semifinal at the French Open. The Polish left-hander, standing 5ft 5in tall, won through intelligence and tactical play rather than raw power, using drop shots and slices to disrupt her opponent's rhythm throughout the match.

Chwalinska's run through qualifying and into the semifinals represents a breakthrough performance at Roland Garros. Her advancement continues her impressive campaign at one of tennis's four major championships.

cards.headline: Artist sues FIFA over destroyed Dallas whale mural ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: A US artist filed a lawsuit seeking $25 million after FIFA covered a Dallas whale mural in preparation for the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
An artist filed a lawsuit against FIFA for $25 million after the organization destroyed or covered a whale mural in Dallas as part of preparations for the 2026 World Cup. The mural was located in Dallas, one of the host cities for the tournament.

The lawsuit centers on the removal or covering of the artwork, which the artist created in Dallas. FIFA is organizing the 2026 World Cup, which will be held across multiple cities in the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The case has surfaced in Dallas federal court.

cards.headline: Alex Scott set to make England debut in World Cup friendlies
cards.teaser: The Bournemouth midfielder is expected to earn his first England cap in upcoming World Cup preparation matches in the United States.
cards.body: Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is poised to make his England debut in the forthcoming World Cup warm-up games in the United States. The friendlies will serve as preparation ahead of the 2026 World Cup, which will be hosted across North America.

cards.headline: Milan Momcilovic transfers to Kentucky basketball from Iowa State
cards.teaser: The former Iowa State player committed to Kentucky through the transfer portal and is scheduled to arrive on campus this weekend.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic, a former Iowa State basketball player, committed to Kentucky through the transfer portal. Momcilovic is scheduled to arrive at Kentucky on Saturday, according to reports.

The addition of Momcilovic prompted Kentucky to appear in updated college basketball rankings. His commitment represents a significant transfer portal acquisition for Kentucky's basketball program. Momcilovic played for Iowa State before entering the transfer portal and choosing to join Kentucky.

hero.headline: CBS News Fires Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes
hero.body:
CBS News has terminated Scott Pelley, a prominent correspondent at 60 Minutes, following a heated confrontation with network management over recent staffing cuts at the program. The firing marks a significant shake-up at one of television's most established news shows.

The dismissal came after Pelley clashed with CBS executives during a Monday morning meeting. According to reports, Pelley objected strongly to decisions made the previous week that removed the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents, Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi, without explanation.

During the tense meeting with newly appointed executive editor Nick Bilton and other CBS News leadership, Pelley directly criticized Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief who joined CBS in October. "She's murdering 60 Minutes," Pelley said, according to accounts of the exchange. "She does not love this place. She was brought in to kill it and is doing exactly that."

CBS management attempted to meet with Pelley after the Thursday terminations, but he was unavailable. On Tuesday, he met with Weiss and other executives, who told him his behavior had been inappropriate. Pelley later told staff members he expected to lose his job.

That same evening, Bilton sent Pelley a message stating he had been "terminated for cause effective immediately." In the message, Bilton referenced Pelley's conduct during the meeting, writing: "Yesterday, you hijacked my first meeting with staff to disparage me, my qualifications, and my intentions with remarkable incivility and contempt."

Bilton subsequently informed 60 Minutes staff of the decision, acknowledging Pelley's importance to the program while defending his actions. "I made repeated attempts to have direct conversations with him over the weekend, and this afternoon I tried to find common ground," he wrote. "That was not the path Scott chose."

Pelley joined CBS News in 1989 and worked on 60 Minutes since 2004, becoming one of the program's most recognizable journalists. He previously anchored the CBS Evening News from 2011 to 2017 and has won numerous awards for his reporting and interviews throughout his decades-long career.

The departures represent substantial changes for 60 Minutes, which has been a cornerstone of CBS News since 1968. With journalist Anderson Cooper announcing earlier this year that he would leave the show, Pelley's firing leaves the program with only three full-time correspondents heading into its 59th season: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and Jon Wertheim. CBS News journalist Norah O'Donnell occasionally contributes to the show.

The network indicated it plans to use correspondents from across its organization more regularly, though no new contributors were immediately named. Bilton told staff he remained committed to supporting them and the show's future journalism.

cards.headline: Spencer Pratt in Second Place in Los Angeles Mayoral Primary
cards.teaser: Reality television personality Spencer Pratt is trailing Mayor Karen Bass in the Los Angeles mayoral primary election.
cards.body:
Spencer Pratt, a reality television personality, finished in second place in the Los Angeles mayoral primary behind incumbent Mayor Karen Bass. The results set up a runoff election in November between Bass and either Pratt or fellow Democrat council member Nithya Raman, depending on final vote tallies.

Pratt has centered his campaign on religious messaging, citing Jesus as his role model. His wife Heidi Montag has publicly supported his candidacy throughout the race.

cards.headline: Martin Scorsese Endorses AI in Filmmaking, Faces Criticism
cards.teaser: Director Martin Scorsese has drawn backlash after praising artificial intelligence as a creative tool for filmmakers.
cards.body:
Acclaimed director Martin Scorsese has become an unlikely advocate for artificial intelligence in filmmaking, drawing both attention and criticism from the entertainment industry. Scorsese's endorsement centers on AI's potential to accelerate the pre-production process while maintaining creative quality.

The director's specific use case involves deploying AI for storyboarding purposes. His comments have generated pushback from those concerned about expanding AI's role in creative work, making Scorsese one of Hollywood's most prominent figures to publicly support the technology's application in film production.

cards.headline: Pink to Host Tony Awards, Promises Stunts
cards.teaser: Grammy-winning singer Pink will host the 79th Tony Awards and says the show will feature stunts.
cards.body:
Pop star Pink will host the 79th Tony Awards this Sunday. The Grammy-winning performer has promised an eventful broadcast, indicating that stunts will be part of the ceremony—and they won't be limited to her alone.

Pink's selection as host raised eyebrows in some circles, a reaction she acknowledged. The artist has noted her background as a theater kid growing up, which connects her to the Broadway community being celebrated at the awards show.

cards.headline: Arsenal's Bukayo Saka to Star in Documentary
cards.teaser: Soccer player Bukayo Saka will be featured in a documentary following Arsenal's Premier League title win.
cards.body:
British soccer star Bukayo Saka is getting a documentary about his life and career. The film, titled Bukayo Saka: The Time is Now, was announced less than two weeks after Arsenal won its first Premier League title since 2004.

Saka, who plays as a forward for Arsenal, was instrumental in the club's championship campaign. He described the documentary as a chance to tell his story in a way he never has before. Saka is considered one of the most gifted British footballers currently playing professionally.

cards.headline: Report Finds Nearly 70 Percent of Americans Play Video Games Weekly
cards.teaser: A new industry report says two-thirds of Americans play video games for at least an hour each week.
cards.body:
Nearly 70 percent of Americans play video games for at least an hour per week, according to a report published by the Entertainment Software Association. The gaming industry lobbying organization said 212.3 million people in the United States between ages 5 and 90 play video games every week.

The report was released Wednesday by the ESA, which represents major companies in the video game industry. The statistics indicate widespread adoption of gaming across age groups in American households.

cards.headline: YouTube Star KSI Leaves Sidemen Group
cards.teaser: Social media personality KSI has quit the Sidemen, a popular YouTube collective.
cards.body:
KSI, a prominent social media star, has left the Sidemen YouTube group. He addressed his former colleagues after his departure from the collective, which has millions of followers on the video platform.

KSI told the remaining Sidemen members that he will always be there for them despite leaving the group. The Sidemen have been one of the most successful YouTube collectives, producing collaborative content for years.

hero.headline: Trump confirms profanity-laced call with Netanyahu over Lebanon
hero.body:
President Trump publicly confirmed Wednesday that he had a heated conversation with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, using strong language to express his frustration over Israel's military operations in Lebanon. Trump made the acknowledgment during an appearance on the New York Post podcast hosted by Miranda Devine.

When Devine asked if Trump had called Netanyahu "fucking crazy" and suggested he would face prison without Trump's support, the president responded affirmatively. "I did," Trump said. "I wouldn't say angry. I was a little bit perturbed at his constantly fighting with Lebanon, you know. At some point I said, 'Bibi, we've got to stop this. We gotta stop it.'"

Trump noted that despite the tension, he maintains positive feelings toward Netanyahu and has worked well with him historically. The conversation reflected Trump's effort to curb Israel's intensified military campaign in the region as he seeks to manage broader tensions with Iran.

The call reveals a significant shift in the public relationship between the two leaders. Trump's willingness to confirm the details rather than deny or minimize the report demonstrates his administration's readiness to apply pressure on Israel regarding its military conduct in Lebanon. Trump appears to view his past support for Netanyahu as leverage in current negotiations.

The exchange occurs amid a complex regional situation. Iran had threatened to suspend peace talks with the United States over Israel's offensive actions in Lebanon. Trump, eager to prevent further escalation and secure a path away from direct confrontation with Iran, reportedly used the profanity-laden call to push Netanyahu toward de-escalation.

The death toll in Lebanon has mounted significantly during the conflict with Israel, reaching 1,422 people according to Lebanese health ministry data. In the 24 hours preceding reports of this call, Israeli strikes killed 54 people and wounded 156 others. These figures underscore the intensity of the military operations that prompted Trump's criticism.

The disagreement over Lebanon marks a notable departure from the strong alignment between Trump and Netanyahu during Trump's first presidency. That period saw the U.S. embassy relocated to Jerusalem and the brokering of the Abraham Accords, which normalized relations between Israel and several Arab nations.

Trump's public confirmation of the tense exchange, rather than attempting to suppress or reframe the story, suggests a calculated diplomatic strategy. By acknowledging the call and his criticism, Trump appears to be signaling to regional actors that he is willing to distance himself from Israeli military decisions when necessary. This approach could serve his effort to prevent further escalation with Iran while maintaining the broader U.S.-Israel relationship.

cards.headline: Steve Hilton, Xavier Becerra lead California governor primary
cards.teaser: Former Fox News host Steve Hilton and former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra were ahead in the race to replace California Gov. Gavin Newsom as vote counting continued.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton was leading California's gubernatorial primary, with Democrat Xavier Becerra and fellow Democrat Tom Steyer in close contention. The race remained too close to call with significant ballots still awaiting tabulation.

California's primary system allows candidates from both parties to compete together, with the top two finishers advancing to the general election regardless of party affiliation. Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer and Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton were vying for their party nominations to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor and could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, a former Biden administration official, won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor on Tuesday. If elected in November, she would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history.

Her primary victory advances her to the general election in a state where Democrats have controlled the governorship since 2011. Haaland's campaign highlighted her federal government experience and leadership as a Native American.

cards.headline: Iowa Senate race shifts to lean Republican after Democratic primary
cards.teaser: The Cook Political Report moved its rating of the Iowa Senate race from likely Republican to lean Republican after state Rep. Josh Turek won the Democratic primary.
cards.body:
The Cook Political Report downgraded its Iowa Senate race rating from likely Republican to lean Republican following Tuesday's Democratic primary results. State Rep. Josh Turek won the primary with nearly 63 percent of the vote, emerging as the establishment-backed candidate.

Turek's primary victory has made the general election more competitive than previously anticipated. The rating shift indicates Democrats now have a realistic path to winning the seat in November.

cards.headline: Cory Booker to face Justin Murphy in New Jersey Senate race
cards.teaser: Sen. Cory Booker secured the Democratic nomination and will face Republican Justin Murphy, a Navy veteran who won his primary despite having virtually no campaign funds.
cards.body:
Sen. Cory Booker won New Jersey's Democratic Senate primary and will face Republican nominee Justin Murphy in November's general election. Both secured victories in Tuesday's primaries.

Murphy, a Navy veteran and former Senate candidate, won a crowded Republican primary despite minimal campaign funding. Booker is seeking another term representing New Jersey in the Senate.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advances to runoff
cards.teaser: Incumbent Mayor Karen Bass secured a spot in the runoff election, though her opponent remained unknown as vote counting continued.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advanced to the November runoff election after winning the primary with less than 50% of the vote. She will face either Republican Spencer Pratt, a former reality TV star, or Democrat Nithya Raman, a city council member, as votes continued to be counted.

Bass is seeking another term as mayor of California's largest city. The final results of the primary could take days to determine, including which candidate will join Bass in the general election.

cards.headline: Federal judge in Atlanta faces pressure over sex scandal
cards.teaser: A federal judge is under growing pressure after an investigation found she lied about an extramarital affair with a police officer and engaged in sexual conduct within earshot of her clerks.
cards.body:
Pressure is mounting on a federal judge after an investigation discovered she lied about being in an extramarital affair with a high-ranking police officer and having sex within earshot of her clerks. The judge, who was appointed during the Obama administration, now faces calls for consequences from multiple quarters.

Lawyers have expressed outrage over the findings. A prominent ethics watchdog is calling for an impeachment inquiry, while the Trump administration hopes to remove her from a key position. The scandal has raised questions about judicial conduct and accountability.
